pairs.question: Non ut illi putant Dauid de ipso referre. Aut si putant illud, congruit uniuersa, quae dixit?
pairs.answer: Non est flagellatus Dauid nec cruce leuatus.
pairs.derivation: The author poses a genuine interrogative (453-455): the Psalms speak of the Lord's death, not, as the Jews think, David referring to himself; or, if they do think that (illud = Dauid de ipso referre, line 454, kept so the question is self-contained), does everything he said fit together? The answer (456) directly answers no by giving the disqualifying fact: David was neither scourged nor crucified. Answer ends at the first full stop (line 456); line 457 turns to a new topic ('Quid? Uaticinantur Iudaei more Saturni'). No scaffolding or editorial brackets in this span.

pairs.question: Quid nobis strident, quid nos aemulantur heredes?
pairs.answer: Fecissentque bonum, et erant in parte legati.
pairs.derivation: A genuine 'why' question posed by the author about the Jews (heredes) snarling at and envying the Christians (nobis); answered (738) with the reason: had they done good, they too would have been among the legatees. Self-contained as a rhetorical complaint and its rebuttal. Answer is the single following line; line 739 ('Nec hodie tacent...') turns to a new statement. No scaffolding or editorial brackets in this span.
